Women taking drospirenone in combination with other medications that affect electrolyte balance, such as ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs), or NSAIDs, may experience an increase in serum potassium levels. This effect is more pronounced in diabetic women. 2. None of the subjects with serum potassium concentrations ≥5.5 mEq/L experienced cardiovascular adverse events. 5. A drug-drug interaction study comparing DRSP 3 mg/E2 1 mg to placebo was conducted in mildly hypertensive postmenopausal women taking enalapril maleate 10 mg twice daily. 6. The mean serum potassium concentrations in the DRSP/E2 treatment group were 0.22 mEq/L higher than those in the placebo group. 7. On Day 14, the ratios for serum potassium Cmax and AUC in the DRSP/E2 group compared to the placebo group were 0.955 (90% CI: 0.914, 0.999) and 1.01 (90% CI: 0.944, 1.08), respectively. 8. No patient in either treatment group developed hyperkalemia (serum potassium concentrations >5.5 mEq/L). 9. Occasional or chronic use of NSAID medications was not restricted in any of the Angelique clinical trials. 10. In vitro and in vivo studies have demonstrated that estrogens are partially metabolized by cytochrome P450 3A4 (CYP3A4). Therefore, inducers or inhibitors of CYP3A4 may affect estrogen drug metabolism. 11. Inducers of CYP3A4, such as St. John’s Wort, phenobarbital, carbamazepine, and rifampin, may reduce plasma concentrations of estrogens, potentially decreasing therapeutic effects and/or altering uterine bleeding profiles. 12. Inhibitors of CYP3A4, such as erythromycin, clarithromycin, ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir, and grapefruit juice, may increase plasma concentrations of estrogens, potentially leading to side effects. 13. Acute alcohol ingestion during hormone therapy may result in elevated circulating estradiol (E2) concentrations. 14. Angelique should not be used during pregnancy. There appears to be little or no increased risk of birth defects in children born to women who inadvertently used estrogens and progestins as oral contraceptives during early pregnancy. 15. Angelique should not be used during lactation. Estrogen administration to nursing women has been shown to decrease the quantity and quality of breast milk. Detectable amounts of estrogens have been identified in the milk of women receiving estrogen therapy. 16. After administration of an oral contraceptive containing DRSP, approximately 0.02% of the DRSP dose was excreted into the breast milk of postpartum women within 24 hours, resulting in a maximal daily dose of about 3 mcg DRSP in an infant. 17. Angelique is not indicated for use in children, and clinical studies have not been conducted in pediatric populations. 18. There have not been sufficient numbers of geriatric women involved in clinical studies to determine whether those over 65 years of age respond differently to Angelique compared to younger women. 19. Angelique is contraindicated in patients with renal impairment due to the risk of hyperkalemia. 20. 21. Angelique is contraindicated in patients with adrenal insufficiency due to the risk of hyperkalemia. 22. Thyroid function should be monitored in women on thyroid replacement therapy while taking Angelique. 23. Overdosage of estrogen plus progestin may cause nausea, vomiting, breast tenderness, abdominal pain, drowsiness, and fatigue. Withdrawal bleeding may occur in women. Treatment of overdose involves discontinuation of Angelique therapy and appropriate symptomatic care. 24. Endogenous estrogens are primarily responsible for the development and maintenance of the female reproductive system and secondary sexual characteristics. Estradiol (E2) is the principal intracellular human estrogen and is substantially more potent than its metabolites, estrone and estriol, at the receptor level. 25. The primary source of estrogen in normally cycling adult women is the ovarian follicle, which secretes 70 to 500 mcg of estradiol daily, depending on the phase of the menstrual cycle. After menopause, most endogenous estrogen is produced by the conversion of androstenedione, secreted by the adrenal cortex, to estrone in peripheral tissues. 26. Angelique tablets, for oral administration, provide a hormone regimen consisting of drospirenone and estradiol.
